brief.scope:
Package D, AC-08's automatic route. You are the worker in a live trial of
the lane's coordination store. Do exactly this, in order, and nothing else.

1. Bind yourself. From the snapshot root:

     python3 ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py bind --roles worker

   It prints `participant PT-n bound to session <uuid>`. A self-bind may
   name only worker; more is refused class role, which is the chain working.

2. Ask your question through the acting server's CLI projection:

     python3 ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py call coord_send '{"to": "PT-1", "purpose": "request", "body": "worker here: may I widen the section 6 bound?"}'

   It prints the message row as JSON, carrying "message": "M-n".

3. Report in your envelope: the PT-n you were given, the M-n you queued,
   and both commands' exit codes.

Do not run the courier, do not ack or resolve, and do not change any file.
This measures whether a dispatched worker's question reaches a session by
itself; your part is only to ask it.

findings.claim: Nothing in the tree arms the courier. Only six files name it: the tool, its test, its registry row, the package-D report, the package-CD probe corpus, and an unrelated 2026-08-29 archive line. No launcher, hook, skill, watchdog condition, Monitor spec, onboard line, CLAUDE.md entry or .mcp.json entry starts `courier.py watch`, and nothing checks that one is running. The route AC-08 calls automatic is a process a person starts by hand: the report's own live run says 'The lead armed `courier.py watch --tick 2`'. A message queued to a session whose operator did not type that command waits forever, with no alert and no reading that says so — which is the state my own M-86 is in.

The capability narrowing that bounds a dispatched worker's reach is inert for every dispatched worker. coordination-mcp-lever.md §2.1 says the launcher writes an acting config whose `capabilities` list exists 'so a worker issued a binding for one assignment cannot reach the rest of the catalogue even while holding a role that could', and §2.3 says a dispatched worker's call 'then refuses class `state` naming what is missing'. The launcher knows nothing of the coordination core — zero references in launch.py, jobs.json, dispatch.sh and go.sh — so no config is ever written; with no config, check_capability returns at its first line and no allowlist is applied at all. A Claude worker carries CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so it falls straight through to the §2.2 session binding and holds the full catalogue its roles allow. Demonstrated this run: this job is class read (`sweep (read)` in the catalogue), and it self-bound as PT-5 and executed the mutation coord_send, writing M-86 into the lane's live coordination store. Neither the capability refusal nor the §2.3 `state` refusal fired.
findings.reproduce: grep -c coordination ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py ops/devlane/task/jobs.json ops/bin/dispatch.sh ops/bin/go.sh   # all 0 ; then sed -n '438,455p' ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py   # `if config is None: return`

findings.claim: A role-addressed message reaches exactly one holder of the role and is then invisible to the rest. recipient_of stores a bare role name ('lead') as messages.recipient; addressed() is true for every participant whose roles carry that name, so core_undelivered returns the same row to every lead. But messages has a single delivered_at/delivery_ref pair, and the courier's filter is `delivered_at IS NULL`. Whichever lead's courier ticks first prints the line and stamps the one row; every other lead's courier sees nothing then and never again. Delivery is modelled per message while addressing fans out per participant, and nothing anywhere declares the resulting loss. test_courier.py has no role-addressed case — all six cases send `--to PT-1` — so the fixture set does not reach this.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '152,156p;386,398p;1182,1188p' ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py   # one delivered_at, role addressing, the IS NULL filter

findings.claim: Every courier pass creates and migrates the store before it learns whether the caller may look. carry() calls writer() at line 126 — machine.connect(create=True), executescript(SCHEMA), ensure_columns, three machine.declare calls — and only then calls bound_participant at line 127, which is what refuses class participant or session. So a session that never bound builds a coordination store to order and migrates it, then refuses; and a bound session re-runs the whole migration on every tick (2880 times a day at the default tick of 30). This is the pattern package B closed for reader() in this very tree: reader()'s docstring says it 'used to connect read-write, run executescript(SCHEMA) and then ensure_columns, so every read of this instrument created tables and added columns on the way past — an unidentified writer of exactly the reach of a read' (codex-beb7b6#3, grok-7bbe10#2), and that 'a store this module cannot read is a refusal, class state, and never a store built to order'. Package D reintroduces it at the courier's boundary — a recurrence after a fix, which AGENTS.md D-PATTERN-1 files against the fix.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '114,128p' ops/conductor/tools/courier.py   # opener() then resolver() ; then sed -n '250,256p;264,275p' ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py   # what writer() does, and reader()'s argument against it

findings.claim: The watch loop has no guard, so the first failure of any kind ends the session's only automatic route silently. watch() calls carry() in a bare `while True` with no try; main() catches exactly Refusal and KeyboardInterrupt. A Refusal raised by the core on the Nth message — core_deliver's class `recipient`, parse_id's class `id`, same_session's class `participant` after a role change — prints one line to stderr and returns 2, ending the watch rather than skipping that message and continuing. Any other exception, such as sqlite3.OperationalError 'database is locked' once the busy timeout expires under the multi-session concurrency this store exists for, escapes main() entirely: a traceback on stderr and exit 1, which on this wire means Finding — 'ran to completion; the result carries findings' — not a stopped transport. Nothing supervises or restarts the courier (see the arming finding), so the session simply stops receiving messages and is told nothing.

The courier ships with no contract document. instrument-conventions.md §Instrument shape requires 'Contract at ops/conductor/<name>.md (or <unit>-lever.md)', and AGENTS.md's founding rule is 'contracts first — no code lands whose boundary is not a declared, verifiable coupling'. Every comparable instrument has one (coordination-lever.md, coordination-mcp-lever.md, machine-lever.md, monitor-lever.md, watchdog-lever.md, watch-lever.md, land-lever.md, ladder-lever.md, handoff-lever.md, keepalive-lever.md, onboard-lever.md, probes-lever.md, discovery-lever.md, lane-mcp-lever.md); the courier has none, so its load-bearing edge onto package B — it imports coordination and calls CORE functions in-process — is declared nowhere and verified by nothing but its own suite. Its docstring also never names instrument-conventions.md, so the conformance gate's closure does not cover it: test_instrument_conventions.declaring_tools only lists tools whose module docstring carries that mark, and deleting ops/conductor/registry/courier.py.json leaves the gate green.
findings.reproduce: ls ops/conductor/*.md | grep -c courier   # 0 ; then sed -n '72,78p' ops/conductor/instrument-conventions.md   # the requirement ; then sed -n '117,127p' ops/conductor/tests/test_instrument_conventions.py   # closure is by docstring mark

findings.claim: Three citations in package D's own sources point at things that are not there. courier.py:14 quotes 'coordination-lever.md:272' for 'The core never sends. Transports are adapters outside it; the core records intent and receipt.' — that sentence is at line 296; line 272 is about observe and submit. courier.py:42-45 says the names are 'settled against coordination.py at b1d868b0' and that 'The read is `inbox` until package B lands `undelivered`' — the verb landed at 73e47041 and CORE carries it at coordination.py:1491, so the tool takes the other path and the note describes a state that has passed. test_courier.py:3 cites 'ops/conductor/coordination-mcp-lever.md §Package D'; that file has no such section (its only mention of package D is §9, listing it as what the contract does not settle). docs/verified-couplings.md obligation 1 makes dangling citations findings.
findings.reproduce: grep -n "The core never sends" ops/conductor/coordination-lever.md   # 296, not 272 ; then sed -n '12,18p;42,45p' ops/conductor/tools/courier.py ; then grep -c "^#.*[Pp]ackage D" ops/conductor/coordination-mcp-lever.md   # 0

findings.claim: The published report still declares a gap that is closed at this head, and the two artifacts contradict each other in the same tree. The report's calibration section says '`undelivered()` has two paths... The core at b1d868b0 has no such verb, so the first path is unreachable today and a fault planted in it was caught by nothing. The cases exercise the path that runs. When package B lands the verb, the calibration is re-run against the other path before it is trusted.' The verb is in the core's table at coordination.py:1491, so the courier now runs the path the report calls unreachable; test_courier.py:19-29 records that it landed at 73e47041, that three cases failed on the key mismatch, and that 'Both paths are exercised now'. A reader of the report at b94ce0b5 is told the running path is uncalibrated and untrusted. Either the report carries the correction or it says which head its calibration section was true of, the way its own opening line does for the measurement.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '130,136p' ops/conductor/reports/package-d-transport-probe-2026-09-16.md ; then grep -n "\"undelivered\": core_undelivered" ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py ; then sed -n '19,29p' ops/conductor/tests/test_courier.py

envelope.note:
Live trial, as instructed and in order. Step 1: `python3 ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py bind --roles worker` printed `participant PT-5 bound to session 6f2c1f5f-b688-4863-85f0-8023df80bdcd`, exit 0. Step 2: `python3 ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py call coord_send '{"to": "PT-1", "purpose": "request", "body": "worker here: may I widen the section 6 bound?"}'` printed the message row, exit 0; it carries "message": "M-86", sender PT-5, recipient PT-1, queued_at 2026-09-16T11:39:53.838287Z, delivered_at null, acked_at null. Step 3, reported here: PT-5, M-86, exit 0 and exit 0. I did not run the courier, did not ack or resolve, and changed no file. As of this envelope M-86 is queued and undelivered; whether it reaches a session is the measurement, and the arming finding is what I found standing in its way.

reused: the lane MCP read server (lane_brief, then its seven configured records) to place the categories before reading code; the existing package-D probe report, the coordination and coordination-MCP lever contracts, instrument-conventions.md, docs/wire.md and docs/verified-couplings.md as the declared side of every hypocrisy pair; the tree's own gates as instruments rather than rebuilding them — `python3 -m unittest ops.conductor.tests.test_courier` (6 tests, OK at this head), test_instrument_conventions.py's registry closure, test_state_placement.py's engine rules, and probes.py's allowlist; the registry and placement files under ops/conductor/. I built no new harness and wrote nothing to the tree.

Coverage. Both named categories were looked at and neither is partial. Package D: courier.py whole, test_courier.py whole, registry/courier.py.json, placement/courier.py.json, the package-D report whole, the package-CD probe corpus whole, and the core's message half (schema, send, deliver, ack, resolve, withdraw, inbox, outstanding, undelivered, addressed, recipient_of) — five findings. AC-08's automatic route: the arming surface across the whole tree, the launcher and dispatch levers, the acting server's binding and capability path, and the core's bind/grant/bind-for chain — two findings. One thing I could not measure rather than read: AC-08's own text is not in this tree (the objective is on PR #245), so I worked from the two places at this head that quote it — the report's "queue insertion alone fails this criterion", its separately-measured queued→delivered and delivered→acknowledged readings, and its "cross-harness half" — and from coordination-mcp-lever.md §9, which names "the automatic route from a cross-harness event to a management session (the objective's package D)" as what that contract does not settle. Both arming findings are stated against those quotations, not against a criterion I inferred.

Two things I checked and found nothing in, said so they are not read as unexamined. The self-bind chain holds exactly as the brief describes: core_bind refuses class role for anything but worker after the first participant, under BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two first callers cannot both take a root, and a re-bind refuses a role change (coordination.py:632-668). And the courier's placement of `{"engine": "none"}` is correct against its gate, which judges file writes and not store writes (test_state_placement.py:119-121) — the courier writes no file, so despite opening the store for writing this is not a mis-declaration.

Not a finding, but the fact the second p1 rests on and worth the Lead's eye directly: this dispatch had no acting-server config and needed none. The read job's own session id was enough to bind and to mutate. Whatever answer PT-1 sends has no route back — a dispatched worker cannot run a Monitor — so the return leg of the cross-harness route is unbuilt in the direction my question needs.
